findings.problem: Column mismatch: the header lists columns Benchmark, Nex-N2-mini, Nex-N2-Pro, GPT-5.5, Opus 4.7, Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.1, MiniMax M3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro (9 cells). The document line has 9 data cells with values 74.4, 80.8, 82.9, 87.6, 80.2, -, 80.5, 80.6 (8 values) after the benchmark-name cell. If this is a right-aligned cell table, the value under Nex-N2-mini is not the first value 74.4 but the value in the model's aligned column. The packet claims column '**Nex-N2-mini**' matched by cell position for 74.4, but with the row carrying one extra leading benchmark-name cell, the model columns shift by one relative to a naive left-to-right read unless the alignment is confirmed. The stated evidence ('matched by cell position') is not sufficient to confirm the 74.4 sits under Nex-N2-mini rather than under Nex-N2-Pro or an off-by-one column.

Column/alignment not adequately evidenced: packet relies on 'cell position' match but the row carries the extra leading benchmark-name cell that shifts model columns; 74.4 may belong to Nex-N2-Pro (80.8) or another column depending on alignment direction.

Insufficient evidence to confirm 34.5 sits under 'Claude Opus 4.7'; header has a single named model with four row values, position unverified.

Header is a family label ('Fable family models Claude Fable 5/ Mythos 5'), not a single-model column. The packet's model as printed for this candidate is 'Claude Fable 5', yet the header names both 'Claude Fable 5' and 'Mythos 5' in one column and the row has three values (54.7, 54.1, 59.4). Whether 54.1 belongs to Claude Fable 5 or to Mythos 5 (or a sibling) cannot be determined from the supplied evidence. This is a column-identity error risk.
Family-level header conflates Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5; cannot confirm 54.1 is Claude Fable 5's own value rather than Mythos 5's.
